label: Onyx & Gilt
description: Near-black and antique gold on warm ivory. Premium without being heavy — suits unisex salons, barbers, grooming studios and any brand whose printed identity is black and gold but whose website has a lot to read.
notes:
Tokens only — sections never hardcode colours, they read these as CSS variables.

WHY LIGHT WHEN THE BUSINESS CARD IS BLACK: this replaced a dark theme built to mirror the card one-to-one. A card is glanced at; a site with sixteen service descriptions and four product pages is read, and long body copy is harder work on near-black. Black-and-gold also signals expensive — right for bridal and keratin, wrong for the everyday haircut that is the volume business. Gold, the near-black headings and the footer carry the identity; the background does not have to.

THE GOLD HAD TO BE DARKENED, AND THIS IS THE WHOLE TRICK: --color-accent is used as 12px meta text in fifteen places, so it must clear WCAG AA at small sizes. The card's actual gold (#C9A227) measures 2.30:1 on this background — unusable. #B08A1E is 3.07:1 and #9C761A is 3.98:1, both still failing. #8F6B18 measures 4.66:1 on the page and 4.90:1 on surface, and is the closest to a true gold that passes. The renderer also derives --color-accent-fg via readableOn(), which puts white on the gold in three places; that pairing measures 4.90:1 and passes too. Do not lighten this towards the card's gold without re-measuring both directions.

Primary is 16.50:1, muted 5.48:1, white-on-primary 17.36:1. Both fonts serve weights 400-700 (checked).
